To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Gal/Gal-NAc-specific lectins are the major adhesins of Entamoeba trophozoites for human enterocytes.
the Gal/GalNac-specific lectin of E. histolytic is transferred to the lateral surface on enterocytes, and that this transfer occurs before killing of the epithelial cells.
Entamoeba histoytica trophozoite contact with epithelial cells in culture resulted in transfer of the ameba lectin to the lateral surface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the hypothesis that amebic lectins are involved in the early steps of amebic invasion of the host.
the identification of amebic molecules that mediate adhesion to and lysis of epithelial cells and with their transfer from trophozoites to the target cells.
the initial steps of amebic pathogenesis and the mechanisms of cell death.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lectin was transferred from trophozoites to the lateral surface, but not to the apical surface, of the enterocyte.
E. histoytica trophozoite-induced target cell lysis involves a contact-dependent transfer of a portion of the amebic Gal/ GalNAc-specific lectins to the target cell surface.

the Gal/GalNac-specific lectin of E. histolytic is a contact dependent transfer molecule which is transferred to the lateral surface epithelial cells in culture and that the transferred lectin is a target of the host immune response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
E. histlytica trophozoite-induced epithelial cell lysis is preceded by a contact-dependent transfer of amebic lectin or lectin fragments to the lateral surface.
E. histoyltica trophozoites transfer the intact lectin or portions of the lectin to the lateral surface epithelial cells in a contact-dependent manner.
the amebic lectin is involved in the initial interaction of E. histolytic with the intestinal epithelium.
The main takeaway from our work is that

E. histoloytica trophozoite transfer of the Gal/GaNAc-specific lectins to the surface of enterocytes occurs before trophozoite killing of the target cells and that the transfer is mediated by the lectin itself.
E. histoloytica trophozoite transfer of Gal/GalNAC-specific lectin is an essential early step in pathogenesis.
E. histolycia trophozoites can transfer a portion of their Gal/GalNAac specific lectin to the lateral surface epithelial cells in culture.
